claims.text: The initial equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi alloy is a single-phase FCC solid solution.
Cyclic mechanical loading at 300–500°C accelerates atomic diffusion in equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Accelerated diffusion under elevated-temperature cyclic loading promotes nanoscale chemical ordering.
Elevated-temperature cyclic loading promotes local compositional fluctuations or segregation.
The proposed segregation occurs particularly at grain boundaries and within the matrix.
Nanoscale ordering and local segregation impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion reduces the alloy's ductility.
Ordered or segregated regions become preferential sites for crack initiation.
The proposed microstructural changes cause premature crack initiation.
Premature crack initiation leads to a marked decrease in toughness.
The proposed ordering and segregation mechanism produces a tendency toward brittle fracture under additional mechanical stress.
Cyclically loaded samples will have lower fracture toughness than both room-temperature baseline samples and elevated-temperature non-loaded controls.
Cyclically loaded samples will have lower elongation to failure than both control groups.
TEM and atom-probe tomography will reveal nanoscale chemical ordering and compositional heterogeneity in the cyclically loaded samples.
Fracture surfaces of the cyclically loaded samples will exhibit cleavage facets or intergranular crack paths characteristic of brittle failure.
The proposed behavior applies at 300–500°C under cyclic stress amplitudes approaching 80% of yield strength.
